_meta.shape_note: Mirrors the AAOIFI GS deep-note shape (display_card + the analytic fields) so BV renders IFSB cards with the same page. id_scheme KB-IFSB-<n>.
_meta.source_text: IFSB-28_En.txt (official IFSB PDF -> txt), 15 Dec 2022 issue. Clause paragraph numbers below are IFSB-28's own numbering, verified-to-text.

notes.standard_name: Revised Solvency Requirements for Takaful / Retakaful Undertakings
notes.issuer: Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB), Kuala Lumpur

display_card.one_liner: How much capital a takaful (Islamic insurance) operator must hold so it can always pay claims.
display_card.what_it_is: A prudential solvency standard for takaful and retakaful firms - the Islamic-insurance counterpart to conventional insurance capital rules, adapted for the two-fund takaful model.
display_card.who_it_applies_to: Regulators supervising takaful, retakaful and takaful-window operations (general, family or composite licences).
display_card.why_it_matters: Solvency is the promise that the mutual fund can pay. It sets the safety margin that protects participants and public confidence.

notes.applicability: Supervisory authorities apply it proportionately to the nature, scale and complexity of the undertaking; a lighter touch is allowed for microtakaful (IFSB-28, para 14).
notes.core_machinery: Two of three sections carry the rules: Section 2 (Valuation) and Section 3 (Regulatory Capital Requirements). Each is built on a Takaful Core Principle from IFSB-27 (Section 2 on TCP 14, Section 3 on TCP 17) and follows the international insurance hierarchy of core principle -> standard -> guidance (IFSB-28, paras 15-16, 726).

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: Capital must be set so a takaful undertaking can meet all contractual obligations with high probability (protection-of-participants objective).
Funds are segregated: a shareholders' fund (SHF) for the operator, and one or more risk-bearing takaful funds (PRF/PIF) for participants' contributions and payouts.

Underwriting surplus of a takaful fund should NOT go to the shareholders' fund (IFSB Shari'ah board, citing the International Fiqh Academy); investment income may partly go to SHF as the mudarib share.
A fund deficit may be covered by a qard from the SHF or a third party, repaid from future surplus; deficits caused by operator negligence/misconduct must be compensated by the operator.
Applies to retakaful and, mutatis mutandis, to takaful windows.

notes.implications: Anchors the takaful/mutual-protection family (F08) at the prudential floor: it is where 'aqilah -> modern takaful lands as a capital rule. Complements AAOIFI SS 26 (Islamic Insurance) and SS 41 (Islamic Reinsurance) - AAOIFI gives the Shari'ah of the contract, IFSB gives the capital math.
notes.limitations: Guidance to regulators, not a contract fiqh standard; expressed for a typical two-tier model and needs modification for other structures (IFSB-28 para 11).
notes.disputes: Surplus disposition and the SHF's entitlement to underwriting surplus remain debated across jurisdictions; IFSB-28 sides with 'no underwriting surplus to SHF' per the Fiqh Academy resolution.
notes.timeline_bridge: aqilah (Q-layer, tribal mutual compensation) -> classical mutual-help fiqh -> 20th c. takaful models -> IFSB-11 (2010) -> IFSB-28 (2022).
